falsifiable_hypothesis: Uniform confidence amplification improves mean error but spends tail margin on low-reliability targets. The patient-count-weighted amplitude shrinker already estimates target deviation amplitude reliability s_j=sqrt(max(0,1-v_j/d_j^2)). Multiplying the global/common union confidence by s_j should focus extra correction on reliable targets.
component_rule: Orientation A is leave-one-whole-patient bagged geometry. Orientation B starts from interpolated-jackknife geometry. No A/B prediction averaging occurs.
shrinkage_rule: Compute theta_weighted, a_global, a_common and target amplitude reliability s_j exactly as in patient_count_weighted_amplitude_js using unique whole-patient counts in each inner fold. Define c_union=1-(1-a_global)*(1-a_common), target amplification m_j=1+c_union*s_j, theta_final,j=m_j*theta_weighted,j, and q_B=q_B,interpolated_jackknife-0.5*theta_final. There is no amplification menu, target/fold outer routing, held-fold outcome use in the canonical rule, or protected data.

task_contract.ab_rule: average losses across separately costed A/B orientations; never average predictions
